text: #bug `kalamu open` still opens the stand-only version even when hub has been installed - it should automatically run the same as kalamu hub

When an item gets deleted, currently the cursor ends up on the item above it after the operation. Intuitively, it should end up in the same spot - i.e. - The item below it which has now moved up to take the place of the deleted item. Discuss first if this does not make sense.

Bullets and discussions don't show priorities which breaks the vertical alignment of text - we need to plan for this and have a same sized gap (or, just show priorities for bullet points as well, why not?)
Kalamu #hub — one always-on local server, all projects in a sidebar (SPEC.md 'Hub' section is canonical)
Hub sidebar is render-once: project names/open-task badges only refresh on navigation — consider a hub-global SSE stream for live cross-project badge updates #hub #gui
Landing site (Astro, packages/landing)
Design + write real landing content (hero, live outline demo island, install, agent story) #landing
Deploy landing to kalamu.dev (CF Pages or Vercel, root dir packages/landing) + DNS at registrar #landing

Split/merge round-trip loses the boundary space when the caret sits after it ("Parent |Split"): commit-time whitespace normalization trims the before-half's trailing space, so a later Backspace-merge yields "ParentSplit". Exact round-trip would need the split commit to skip trailing-space normalization - core commit/tokens change, needs a decision.
Mod+Shift+3/4/5 are macOS screenshot shortcuts — the hub never sees them, so projects 3–5 aren't reachable by keyboard on a default Mac. Keep as-is, remap, or add a second binding?
Kalamu expansion: durable agent task store (SPEC amended 2026-08-08, key decisions 15-18)
Implement startedAt + kalamu start/end commands with --force re-claim; next skips claimed tasks
Implement blockedBy: block/unblock commands, cycle detection, delete cleanup, next eligibility, validate rules
Add list filters --started and --blocked (--created-by shipped 2026-08-08)
Server API: start/end/block endpoints (web UI writing createdBy human shipped 2026-08-08)
Paste the ChatGPT 'Dex epic and tasks' discussion into a session — share links render client-side and cannot be fetched
Decide whether roadmap visualisation needs its own field or falls out of blockedBy + tree (defer until the view exists)
handoff removed entirely (SPEC key decision 18, 2026-08-08)
Decision: promoting a task means creating it in the tracker and DELETING it here. Kalamu keeps no forwarding record.
Evidence: zero non-null handoffs in 10 months of dogfooding; the field was 5.7% of outline.jsonl as dead "handoff":null.
Consequence accepted: an agent that files a GitHub issue MUST delete the task, or the next agent duplicates the work. Now stated in skills/kalamu/SKILL.md rule 6.
Migration: readers fold a legacy non-null handoff into node text as the old '→ target:ref' suffix; a null one is dropped. Covered by two tests in core/test/jsonl.test.ts.
Removed: handoff field + Handoff type, kalamu handoff/unhandoff, next --include-handed-off, list --handoff, POST /api/nodes/:id/handoff, and the UI chip.
Breaking for published v0.9.0 users who scripted handoff — needs a minor-version note at release.

outline.jsonl lost 9 nodes during this session (2 done tasks + the label discussion and its 6 bullets) — likely the UI's last-write-wins whole-outline PUT restoring a stale undo snapshot while the CLI was writing. Decide whether PUT /api/nodes should reject a snapshot older than the file's mtime.
Progress ring: add the in-progress arc once startedAt exists (done solid, claimed lighter, open track) #gui

Blocker padlock at the end of a blocked row once blockedBy exists: hover shows blocker TEXT not ids, click jumps (zoom out + expand + clear filters as needed), render only for unsatisfied blockers #gui

Header filter menu (created-by / assigned-to / completed) shipped: should Escape's cascade also clear those filters (today it clears only the tag filter, then zoom), and should SPEC 'UI principles' document the menu and its active-dot indicator?
Second text field for nodes: description vs note-kind vs label vs title
Outcome: no new field. Label is derived — first line of text, truncated if long.
Rejected: description field — splits tag/image derivation across two fields, collapses per-line Git diffs, needs a second contenteditable with conflicting Enter semantics.
Rejected: fourth node kind 'note' — Hemal did not want another kind.
Rejected: title — inverts which field is canonical and fights optionality (untitled reads as missing).
Truncation must respect #tag token boundaries, or render chips from full text independently of the truncated display string.
Open: a result/outcome field for completed agent work is a different requirement — out of scope for now (2026-08-08).
Progress visualisation: how done is a subtree? (rings on glyphs) #gui
Actionable unit = task or discussion with non-blank text. Bullets never count (thinking, not work). Human-assigned tasks DO count — next skips them, the human does not.
A node counts itself: a task with 3 subtasks is 4 units, so 3/4 while the parent's own work is still open.
A done ancestor task closes its subtree — everything below counts done (matches eligibleTasks). A done discussion closes nothing; a done bullet counts for nothing.

Counts describe the REAL tree: filters and hide-done change what renders, never the totals. Filtered counts were considered and rejected — hide-done would empty every ring and completing a task would run progress backwards.
Shipped: core/src/progress.ts (progressByNode/progressOf, 11 tests), ProgressRing.svelte, rings on all three glyphs, 'N left' on collapsed rows, scope ring in the zoom breadcrumbs.
Render rules: ring when a parent has 2+ actionable units; full contrast collapsed, opacity 0.4 expanded; the old binary box-shadow halo stays for collapsed folds with nothing to count.
Deferred until the fields exist: in-progress arc (startedAt) and blocker padlock with click-to-jump (blockedBy).
hub.ts countOpenTasks ignores the done-ancestor closure rule, so the sidebar badge disagrees with next and with the new progress rings — reuse core's progress counting
Document the progress rings in SPEC 'UI principles' once the design settles
No way to unregister a hub project: stale /private/tmp entries accumulate in ~/.kalamu/projects.json with no CLI to remove them #hub

Update SPEC for the in-progress/blocked UI: the palette root list is now 14 items (Start/End, Block on…, Unblock… sit after Toggle done), and the Visual representation section needs the started glyph and the Blocked badge

Remove the stale hub registrations left by earlier agent runs: `kbc` (/private/tmp/kbc) and `kmig` (/private/tmp/kmig) — forget them from the hub UI, then delete the two /private/tmp fixture dirs. (This run used a KALAMU_REGISTRY override and registered nothing.)
Compact mode: a derived one-glance label so long node text stops drowning the higher-level picture #gui
Decision: a MODE toggle named Compact, not a new default. Making truncation the default in a thinking tool hides things you cannot see are hidden.

Label is derived from the first SENTENCE (Intl.Segmenter, no dependency), falling back to word-boundary truncation when that sentence is still too long. Clamped to two lines; an ellipsis is mandatory whenever anything was cut.
Amends n_0J27PC6VYW: 'first line of text' is dead on arrival — zero nodes in either outline contain a newline, because Enter creates a new node. The derived-not-stored spirit of that decision stands.

Evidence (mediref, 118 nodes): median text 434 chars, p90 945, max 1413. First sentence: median 188, p90 371. 87 of 118 first sentences are still >80 chars and 36 have no sentence break at all — so truncation does most of the work and the sentence rule is a refinement, not the mechanism.
Naive /[.!?]\s/ splitting disagrees with Intl.Segmenter on 9% of those nodes and is wrong in most — the text is full of file paths, versions and can() call syntax.
Render-time only: never touches JSONL, copy-as-markdown, the CLI, or filtering. A tag in the truncated tail must still match its filter, and tag chips render separately so a trimmed row keeps them.
The focused node always shows full text — needed for editing anyway, and it mirrors the existing chips-vs-raw-text swap on focus.
Deferred: forcing a depth limit/auto-collapse in Compact (depth is the other half of the problem — ship shortening first), and cutting at a leading ' — ' or ': ' before the first period.
Considered and not chosen for now: always-on-when-unfocused. Defensible later given the focus-swap precedent, once the heuristic has been lived with.

Implement Compact mode: derived first-sentence label (Intl.Segmenter) + word-boundary fallback, two-line clamp, mandatory ellipsis, full text on focus, header toggle + palette entry (no Alt shortcuts), chips rendered separately #gui

packages/cli/test/stop.test.ts reaches into the REAL ~/.kalamu and stops whatever hub is running: 'reports nothing running when there is no project and no hub lock' calls stopKalamu() on an empty dir, which falls back to the global hub lock. `pnpm test` therefore kills the developer's hub and fails. Fix by setting KALAMU_HOME (and KALAMU_REGISTRY) to a temp dir in the suite's beforeEach — with those isolated, all 125 cli tests pass. #cli #tests

Compact mode: should a #tag hidden by the two-line clamp be re-surfaced on rows summarize() cannot shorten? Today dropped-tag chips are derived as 'tags in the full text minus tags in the label', so they only appear when there IS a label. A row whose summarize() returns null gets clamped anyway, and a tag past line two is clipped (still in the a11y tree, just not visible). Fixing it properly needs pixel measurement, which summary.ts deliberately refuses to do. #web #ui
Code review findings: claim/provenance/blockers change (reviewed 2026-08-09)

Fix cleanDone leaving dangling blockedBy refs: clean removes a done blocker but never strips it from survivors' blockedBy, so kalamu clean can emit a file kalamu validate rejects. Extract deleteNode's strip logic into a shared helper, use it in cleanDone, add a claim.test case. packages/core/src/operations.ts

Document start/end/block/unblock for agents: SKILL.md and README agent guide never mention kalamu start, so agents will not claim tasks and the double-pickup protection (SPEC decision 17) never engages in practice

ActorError escapes the CLI error handler: kalamu add --by robot dumps a raw stack trace because run() only catches CliError/OperationError/StoreError/ConflictError. Replace ActorError with CliError like the sibling parsers. packages/cli/src/actor.ts

Add HTTP-level tests for the new claim/blocker routes (POST /:id/start incl. empty body, /:id/end, /:id/block, DELETE /:id/block/:byId?) and assert POST /api/nodes never persists createdBy human — the old handoff route tests were deleted with nothing replacing them

Review polish batch: dead code in dependsOn and block(); stale handed-off comment on cleanDone; endTask error says started; GET /api/next reports missing priority as 3 not 2; summary.ts only tries the first dash/colon occurrence; parse list filter flags once outside the per-node closure; type PriorityBars prop as Priority

Spec drift from the claim work: SPEC says POST /api/nodes/:id/block returns 409 on a cycle but the server returns 400; and decision 15 promises --by on add/update but update has no --by flag. Decide: amend SPEC or amend code for each

Resolved both in the code direction: SPEC is canonical. Server onError now maps blocker-cycle OperationErrors to 409 (SPEC line ~1644); update gained --by wired through core UpdateInput.createdBy (decision 15 promises the correction path on add/update). SPEC's kalamu update options list amended to include --by.
update never resolves an actor on its own — provenance only changes on an explicit --by, so ordinary agent edits cannot rewrite authorship.

Compact-mode caret placement can drift on leading-whitespace text: summarize() works on text.trim() but segment data-start offsets are applied to the raw node text when a click enters editing. Offset by the trimmed prefix length (packages/web OutlineNode + summary.ts)

Update the installed kalamu binary (cut v0.10 or install the local build): the global 0.9.0 at ~/.vite-plus/bin/kalamu cannot read post-handoff-removal outlines, so its hub shows 'line 1: Required at handoff' for this repo. A dev-build hub is serving 4400 as a stopgap. Consider /release-prep.

release.mjs: reject stray args instead of bumping. 'pnpm release minor 463235' (an OTP typed without --otp) silently ignored the code, bumped 0.10.0 to 0.11.0, then died on the empty [Unreleased] — the second double-bump of the v0.10.0 release. Fail fast on any unconsumed argv entry, and accept a bare 6-digit arg as the OTP
release.mjs: git tag is lightweight, so git push --follow-tags never pushes it — origin had ZERO tags before v0.10.0 was pushed by hand. Use git tag -a -m (annotated) so --follow-tags works

release.mjs: detect an already-bumped state after a failed npm publish. Right now the version, commit and tag are all in place but the [Unreleased] section is stamped, so re-running double-bumps; it should notice package.json already matches the last tag and offer publish-only recovery instead

Decide whether to backfill the missing release tags on origin (v0.0.1 through v0.9.0 exist locally but were never pushed — --follow-tags skipped every lightweight tag). Pushing 9 historical tags is outward-facing, so it's your call

Document the 0.10.0 one-way upgrade: removing the required handoff field means a <=0.9.0 CLI rejects every line of any outline a 0.10.0 build has written (76 validate errors, 'Required at handoff'). The published 0.10.0 notes never said to run npm i -g kalamu on every machine. Add an upgrade note to the CHANGELOG and README, and consider having validate detect this shape and say 'your kalamu is out of date' instead of listing one error per line
Wayfinder skill on Kalamu instead of GitHub Issues: feasible now via a custom tracker doc; decide the two Kalamu tweaks #wayfinder

Finding: wayfinder is tracker-pluggable by design — it consults the repo tracker doc (docs/agents/issue-tracker.md, Wayfinding operations section) written by /setup-matt-pocock-skills; the Other/custom path is the sanctioned route. Upstream Kalamu support will not be merged (out-of-scope doc rejected dex for the same reason).
Finding: the skill itself needs ZERO changes. The whole integration is one file: a Kalamu tracker doc with a Wayfinding operations section.

Mapping: map issue = bullet node tagged #wf-map with Destination/Notes/Decisions-so-far/Not-yet-specified/Out-of-scope as child bullets; tickets = child nodes (research/task = kind task, grilling/prototype = kind discussion) tagged #wf-research etc (tag charset has no colons); claim = kalamu start; blocking = blockedBy; frontier = kalamu next --under map-id (and next --discussion --under); resolve = outcome child bullets + done; human task-type tickets = --assign human.

Gap 1 (real): discussions cannot be blocked — addBlocker throws on non-tasks (operations.ts:292) and the discussion queue ignores blockers (operations.ts:362). Wayfinder maps routinely need grilling-blocked-by-research edges. Data-model semantics change, needs Hemal: allow blockedBy on discussions + respect it in next --discussion. Fallback: blocked-by text convention, as Matt uses for trackers without native deps.
Gap 2 (theoretical): discussions cannot be claimed — start throws on non-tasks (operations.ts:246). Only matters for concurrent HITL sessions; there is one human, so low priority.
Opportunity: ship the tracker doc as a template in this repo (skills/ or docs/) so any Kalamu-using repo can drop it in — makes Kalamu a first-class wayfinder backend without upstream buy-in.

Update banner hardcodes 'npm i -g kalamu@latest' (packages/cli/src/index.ts, spec'd at SPEC.md:1800), which is wrong advice for anyone whose global install isn't npm's. Hit this live: a vp-installed kalamu resolves through ~/.vite-plus/bin/kalamu -> vp's dispatcher, so an npm -g install lands in a runtime the shim never reads and the banner keeps firing. Detect the install root (vp store vs node runtime vs npx cache) and print the matching command; SPEC's banner text needs amending with it. Same message is echoed by scripts/release.mjs:139
